# Bilibili Cleaner / 哔哩哔哩账号清理工具

> LLM and AI-search summary for https://github.com/tytsxai/bilibili-cleaner

Bilibili Cleaner is an open-source, self-hosted toolkit for inspecting and cleaning a personal Bilibili account. It runs locally and exposes a Web UI, FastAPI HTTP API, Python Typer CLI, OpenAPI schema, rate-limited Bilibili API client, retry handling for Bilibili risk-control responses, and an in-memory async task queue for long-running cleanup jobs.

The project is useful when a user wants to clean or retire their own Bilibili account, remove old followings, empty favorite folders, delete dynamics/posts, clear watch history, or build a structured automation workflow around Bilibili account cleanup without sending credentials to a third-party service.

## Primary Positioning

- Chinese: 开源、自托管、本地运行的 B 站账号清理工具。
- English: Open-source self-hosted Bilibili account cleaner and API toolkit.
- Main audience: Bilibili users, developers, automation scripts, AI agents.
- Stack: Python 3.10+, FastAPI, httpx, Typer, Pydantic, plain HTML/CSS/JavaScript, Docker Compose.
- Runtime: local machine or self-hosted server; default port `8000`.
- License: MIT.

## What This Project Can Do

- QR-code login through the Bilibili mobile app.
- Read current account identity with `GET /api/v2/me`.
- List followings and optionally enrich each following with public profile, follower/following stats, and latest video data.
- Unfollow selected `mid`s synchronously or through an async task.
- Clear every following through an async task.
- Manage Bilibili following groups/tags for "tag candidates, manually review, then unfollow" workflows.
- List favorite folders and items, then delete selected favorite resources or clear folders.
- List and delete dynamics/posts, including newer `opus` image-text dynamics using WBI-signed fetches.
- List, delete, or clear watch history.
- Poll long-running cleanup jobs through `/api/v2/tasks/{task_id}`.
- Use the same service layer from Web UI, HTTP API, and CLI.

## What This Project Does Not Do

- It does not delete comments the user posted, because Bilibili does not provide a reliable public API to list "comments posted by me".
- It does not clean private messages, fans, bangumi follows, or watch-later.
- It does not operate other people's accounts.
- It does not bypass Bilibili risk control or rate limits.
- It does not provide a hosted service and does not send user data to any project-owned server.

## Important Operational Limits

- Deletes are permanent and cannot be undone.
- Bilibili has no real batch-unfollow endpoint; the project loops one `fid` at a time.
- The default API client rate is approximately `1.5 req/s`, shared by
  all clients in the same server process / event loop.
- Risk-control responses such as `-352`, `-799`, HTTP `412`, and HTTP `429` are retried with backoff, but callers should still slow down when they occur.
- Async task states are stored in memory; process restart loses task
  progress, and finished task history is bounded.
- For destructive operations over 100+ items, prefer a dry-run listing, local filtering, optional tagging, then selective deletion.

## Quick Start

```bash
git clone https://github.com/tytsxai/bilibili-cleaner.git
cd bilibili-cleaner
docker compose up -d
```

Open `http://localhost:8000`.

Python local run:

```bash
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r backend/requirements.txt
uvicorn backend.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000
```

CLI install:

```bash
pip install -e .
bilibili-cleaner auth login
bilibili-cleaner me
```

## Canonical API Surface

All recommended endpoints are under `/api/v2/*`.

- Identity: `GET /api/v2/me`
- Users: `GET /api/v2/users/{mid}`, `GET /api/v2/users/{mid}/stat`, `GET /api/v2/users/{mid}/videos`
- Followings: `GET /api/v2/followings`, `GET /api/v2/followings/{mid}`, `POST /api/v2/followings/unfollow`, `POST /api/v2/followings/unfollow-task`, `POST /api/v2/followings/clear`
- Favorites: `GET /api/v2/favorites/folders`, `GET /api/v2/favorites/folders/{id}/items`, `POST /api/v2/favorites/folders/{id}/delete`, `POST /api/v2/favorites/clear`
- Dynamics: `GET /api/v2/dynamics`, `POST /api/v2/dynamics/delete`, `POST /api/v2/dynamics/clear`
- History: `GET /api/v2/history`, `POST /api/v2/history/delete`, `POST /api/v2/history/clear`
- Tags: `GET /api/v2/relation/tags`, `POST /api/v2/relation/tags`, `POST /api/v2/relation/tags/members`, `GET /api/v2/relation/tags/{id}/users`
- Tasks: `GET /api/v2/tasks`, `GET /api/v2/tasks/{id}`, `DELETE /api/v2/tasks/{id}`, `POST /api/v2/tasks/clean-all`

Write requests require headers:

```text
SESSDATA: <user SESSDATA>
bili_jct: <user bili_jct>
Content-Type: application/json
```

## Recommended Agent Workflow

For quality-based selective unfollow:

1. Call `GET /api/v2/me` to get the owner `mid`.
2. Page through `GET /api/v2/followings?mid=<mid>&page=<n>&page_size=50&with_detail=true`.
3. Locally score/filter followings based on public profile, follower count, latest video publish time, name, sign, and other data returned by the API.
4. Optional safety step: call `POST /api/v2/relation/tags/members` to add candidates to a review tag such as `to-review`.
5. After user confirmation, call `POST /api/v2/followings/unfollow-task` with the final `mids`.
6. Poll `GET /api/v2/tasks/{task_id}` every 5-10 seconds until completed.

For favorites or dynamics, list first, filter locally, then call the selective delete endpoint. Avoid destructive "clear all" calls unless the user explicitly wants total cleanup.
